name: Falcon 9 Block 5

stages.source: https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf ("Nine SpaceX M1D engines power the Falcon 9 first stage")
https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf ("A single Merlin Vacuum (MVac) engine powers the second stage")

note: The real two-stage vehicle. GOES-R flew on an Atlas V 541, not a Falcon 9; it is used here as a GTO-class payload already in the dataset. The second-stage tank is below the app's 4 % dry-mass rule (3.2 %), so the app flags it.

name: Saturn V (Apollo 11, AS-506)

stages.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19750063889/downloads/19750063889.pdf (MSFC-MAN-503: "The S-IC stage (figure 4-1) is a cylindrical booster, 138 feet long and 33 feet in diameter, powered by five liquid propellant F-1 rocket engines.")

https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19750063889/downloads/19750063889.pdf (MSFC-MAN-503: "The stage (figure 5-1) is 81.5 feet long, 33 feet in diameter, and is powered by five liquid propellant J-2 rocket engines")
https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19750063889/downloads/19750063889.pdf (MSFC-MAN-503: "The Saturn S-IVB (figure 6-1) is the third booster stage. Its single J-2 engine ...")

note: Stage masses are Apollo 11 (AS-506) actuals. The app's engine-fit rule allows 4 F-1 on the S-IC; the real stage flew 5 (evaluateBuild does not enforce the fit rule). The app treats the S-IVB as one burn; the real S-IVB burned twice (orbit insertion, then trans-lunar injection).

name: Atlas V 401

stages.source: https://www.ulalaunch.com/rockets/atlas-v ("the liquid oxygen/liquid kerosene, two-thrust-chamber RD-180 engine is a complete propulsion unit"; one RD-180 per booster, two thrust chambers)

https://www.ulalaunch.com/docs/default-source/rockets/atlasvusersguide2010.pdf (Fig. 1.4.1-3: "Thrust: 99.2 kN (22,300 lbf) (SEC)"; "Inert Mass: 4X1: 2,243 kg", the single-engine Centaur the tank record uses); https://www.ulalaunch.com/rockets/atlas-v ("a Centaur upper stage in a single- or dual-engine configuration")

note: 401 = 4-m fairing, no solid boosters, single-engine Centaur. GOES-R itself flew on a 541 (5-m fairing, four solids); the dataset has no solid boosters, so the 401 carries it here.

name: Delta IV core + 5-m upper stage

stages.source: https://www.ulalaunch.com/docs/default-source/rockets/delta-iv-user's-guide.pdf ("The first-stage CBC is powered by the Rocketdyne RS-68A engine")
https://www.ulalaunch.com/docs/default-source/rockets/delta-iv-user's-guide.pdf ("Both second stages use the cryogenic Pratt & Whitney Rocketdyne (PWR) RL10B-2 engine")

note: Not a flown configuration: the 5-m second stage flew only on the Delta IV M+(5,2), M+(5,4) and Heavy, i.e. always with solid motors or side cores (Delta IV User's Guide 2013: "5-m version used on the Delta IV M+(5,2), Delta IV M+(5,4), and Delta IV Heavy"). The dataset has no solid motors, so this is the core vehicle alone. Nova-C flew on Falcon 9.

name: Team demo build

stages.source: https://www.spacex.com/assets/media/falcon-users-guide-2025-05-09.pdf ("Nine SpaceX M1D engines power the Falcon 9 first stage")
https://www.ulalaunch.com/docs/default-source/rockets/delta-iv-user's-guide.pdf ("Both second stages use the cryogenic Pratt & Whitney Rocketdyne (PWR) RL10B-2 engine")

note: The team app's demo story, not a real vehicle: a Falcon 9 first stage under a Delta IV 5-m hydrolox upper stage, sending the stowed JWST toward the Moon. Every part is a real record.
